* Compare multidicts such as `FormData` and `QueryParams` by key while keeping the order of values under a repeated key, so `FormData` with repeated uploads no longer raises `TypeError`. `QueryParams("a=1&a=2")` and `QueryParams("a=2&a=1")` are no longer equal [#3619](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3619).
* Build URL-encoded form fields in the parser callbacks, lowering memory and CPU usage for forms with many fields [#3724](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3724).
* Compare `Match` members by identity during routing [#3665](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3665) and [#3722](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3722).
* Deprecate `starlette.formparsers.FormMessage`, which is no longer used [#3724](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3724).
* Parse the last URL-encoded form field when the request stream ends without an empty chunk [#3599](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3599).
* Keep path parameter values that look like another placeholder in `url_path_for()` [#3725](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3725).
* Default omitted `http.response.start` headers in `BaseHTTPMiddleware`, `GZipMiddleware` and `SessionMiddleware` instead of raising `KeyError` [#3721](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3721).
* Clear the traceback of handled exceptions, so reused exception instances no longer keep per-request objects alive [#3205](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3205).
* Strip only one pair of matching outer quotes from `Config` env file values [#3720](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3720).
* Strip `root_path` from `PATH_INFO` only at a path segment boundary in `WSGIMiddleware` [#3718](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3718).
* Report NaN and infinity correctly in `FloatConvertor.to_string()` [#3716](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3716).
* Ignore `Range` on requests other than `GET` and `HEAD` in `FileResponse` [#3679](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3679).

* Stream `TestClient` response bodies, so `client.stream()` returns before the application finishes. Closing an unfinished streamed response now cancels the application [#3491](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3491).
* Percent-encode `?`, `#`, `\` and a leading `//` in the request path when building `request.url`, and `\` and a leading `//` in `url_path_for` [#3671](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3671).
* Use the byte length for `Content-Length` when the response body is a typed or multidimensional `memoryview` [#3622](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3622).
* Include `HEAD` in the `Allow` header of `HTTPEndpoint` 405 responses when `GET` is defined [#3585](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3585).
* Match host names case-insensitively in `Host` routing and `TrustedHostMiddleware` [#3542](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3542).
* Preserve every existing `Vary` header in `MutableHeaders.add_vary_header()`, used by `GZipMiddleware` and `SessionMiddleware` [#3675](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3675).
This release drops Python 3.10 support and adds HTTP 103 Early Hints.
* Add `Request.send_early_hints()` for HTTP 103 Early Hints through the ASGI `http.response.early_hint` extension [#3435](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3435).
* Require Python 3.11 or later, dropping support for Python 3.10 [#3592](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3592).
* Exclude native gRPC media types (`application/grpc` and `application/grpc+...`) from `GZipMiddleware` compression by default [#3565](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3565).

* Send `http.response.start` immediately in `GZipMiddleware` for responses with an existing `Content-Encoding`, status `206`, or an excluded content type, instead of waiting for the first body chunk [#3631](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3631).
* Resolve the multipart charset once per request instead of once per field [#3618](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3618).
* Stop `FileResponse` transfers when the client disconnects [#3523](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3523).
* Stop multipart range responses when the file ends before a range is complete, instead of looping forever [#3583](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3583).
* Ignore `Range` when `If-Range` contains a weak ETag [#3567](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3567).
* Close `Request.stream()` generators deterministically, avoiding "Exception ignored" errors with stacked `BaseHTTPMiddleware` [#3628](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3628).
* Add `Vary: Cookie` when `Session.pop()` removes an existing key [#3186](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3186).
* Emit `Max-Age=0` on the session cookie when `SessionMiddleware` uses `max_age=0` [#3651](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3651).
This release adds experimental OpenTelemetry tracing and requires AnyIO 4.
Its API and emitted telemetry may change in minor releases without a deprecation period

* Add experimental `OpenTelemetryMiddleware` for HTTP server spans, with URL exclusions and custom tracer providers [#3438](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3438), [#3463](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3463), and [#3520](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3520).
* Support the `QUERY` HTTP method in `HTTPEndpoint`, CORS, and OpenAPI 3.2 schema generation [#3489](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3489).
* Capture HTTP response trailers in `TestClient` and expose them through `response.extensions["http.response.trailers"]` [#3563](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3563).
* Add `partitioned` to `Response.delete_cookie()` on Python 3.14 and later [#3376](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3376).
* Raise `WebSocketDisconnected`, a `RuntimeError` subclass, for disconnected WebSocket operations [#2767](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/2767).
* Accept `Collection[str]` in `CORSMiddleware` configuration annotations, including sets and frozensets [#3518](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3518).
* Run background tasks only after the response is sent when using `BaseHTTPMiddleware` [#3476](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3476).
* Return `400` for invalid multipart parser input [#3492](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3492).

* Include `Vary: Origin` on all normal CORS responses and vary preflight responses by all request headers that affect them [#3516](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3516) and [#3517](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3517).
* Handle malformed `Host` headers and IPv6 authorities consistently across URL construction, host routing, and redirect middleware [#3472](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3472).
* Ignore `Range` headers when `FileResponse` has a status other than `200`, preserving its status and full body [#3568](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3568).
* Reject WebSocket requests to `StaticFiles` without raising an assertion error [#3532](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3532).
* Persist session mutations made with `popitem()` and `|=` [#3436](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3436).
* Handle empty and absent payloads in `WebSocketEndpoint.decode()` [#3372](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3372).
* Allow `HTTPException` to use non-standard status codes without an explicit `detail` [#3545](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3545).

* Avoid deprecated AnyIO imports in `TestClient` and add explicit imports in `WSGIMiddleware` for AnyIO 4.15 compatibility [#3498](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3498) and [#3501](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3501).
* Offload debug traceback rendering to a worker thread in `ServerErrorMiddleware` [#2858](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/2858).
* Expand default excluded content types in `GZipMiddleware` [#3421](https://github.com/encode/starlette/pull/3421).
* Flush GZip output for each streamed chunk [#3419](https://github.com/encode/starlette/pull/3419).
* Skip compression of partial responses in `GZipMiddleware` [#3420](https://github.com/encode/starlette/pull/3420).
* Default `thread_minimum_size` to 128 KiB in `GZipResponder`, keeping it usable without the new keyword argument [#3415](https://github.com/encode/starlette/pull/3415).

* Offload large GZip compression to a worker thread, keeping the event loop responsive. `GZipMiddleware` accepts a new `thread_minimum_size` parameter (default 128 KiB) controlling the minimum body chunk size compressed in a thread [#3410](https://github.com/encode/starlette/pull/3410).
* Use `zlib.compressobj` instead of `GzipFile` in `GZipMiddleware`, reducing memory usage during compression [#3411](https://github.com/encode/starlette/pull/3411).
* Lazily allocate `GZipMiddleware` compression resources, avoiding compressor allocation for responses that are never compressed [#3407](https://github.com/encode/starlette/pull/3407).
* Catch `OSError` alongside `MultiPartException` when closing temp files [#3191](https://github.com/encode/starlette/pull/3191).
* Avoid collapsing exception groups raised from user code [#2830](https://github.com/encode/starlette/pull/2830).
* Use `removeprefix` to strip the weak `ETag` indicator in `is_not_modified` [#3193](https://github.com/encode/starlette/pull/3193).
* Fix `IndexError` in `URL.replace()` on a URL with no authority [#3317](https://github.com/encode/starlette/pull/3317).
* Use `httpx2` for type checking in the `testclient` module [#3304](https://github.com/encode/starlette/pull/3304).
* Add assert error for `requires()` when the request parameter is not a `Request` type [#3298](https://github.com/encode/starlette/pull/3298).
* Support httpx2 in the test client [#3291](https://github.com/encode/starlette/pull/3291).
* Use `"application/octet-stream"` as the `FileResponse` media type fallback [#3283](https://github.com/encode/starlette/pull/3283).
* Only dispatch standard HTTP verbs in `HTTPEndpoint` [#3286](https://github.com/encode/starlette/pull/3286).

Adds appropriate [CORS headers](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/CORS) to outgoing responses in order to allow cross-origin requests from browsers.
The default parameters used by the CORSMiddleware implementation are restrictive by default,
so you'll need to explicitly enable particular origins, methods, or headers, in order
for browsers to be permitted to use them in a Cross-Domain context.
* `allow_origins` - A list of origins that should be permitted to make cross-origin requests. eg. `['https://example.org', 'https://www.example.org']`. You can use `['*']` to allow any origin.

* `allow_origin_regex` - A regex string to match against origins that should be permitted to make cross-origin requests. eg. `'https://[a-zA-Z0-9-]+\.example\.org'`. Avoid using `.*` or `.+` as they match URL special characters (`/`, `@`, `#`, `?`) and may result in overly permissive origin matching. Use specific character classes like `[a-zA-Z0-9-]+` instead.
* `allow_methods` - A list of HTTP methods that should be allowed for cross-origin requests. Defaults to `['GET']`. You can use `['*']` to allow all standard methods.

* `allow_headers` - A list of HTTP request headers that should be supported for cross-origin requests. Defaults to `[]`. You can use `['*']` to allow all headers. The `Accept`, `Accept-Language`, `Content-Language` and `Content-Type` headers are always allowed for CORS requests.

* `allow_credentials` - Indicate that cookies should be supported for cross-origin requests. Defaults to `False`. Also, `allow_origins`, `allow_methods` and `allow_headers` cannot be set to `['*']` for credentials to be allowed, all of them must be explicitly specified.
* `allow_private_network` - Indicates whether to accept cross-origin requests over a private network. Defaults to `False`.
* `expose_headers` - Indicate any response headers that should be made accessible to the browser. Defaults to `[]`.
* `max_age` - Sets a maximum time in seconds for browsers to cache CORS responses. Defaults to `600`.
The middleware responds to two particular types of HTTP request...
These are any `OPTIONS` request with `Origin` and `Access-Control-Request-Method` headers.
In this case the middleware will intercept the incoming request and respond with
appropriate CORS headers, and either a 200 or 400 response for informational purposes.
Any request with an `Origin` header. In this case the middleware will pass the

Private Network Access is a browser security feature that restricts websites from public networks from accessing servers on private networks.
When a website attempts to make such a cross-network request, the browser will send a `Access-Control-Request-Private-Network: true` header in the
pre-flight request. If the `allow_private_network` flag is set to `True`, the middleware will include the `Access-Control-Allow-Private-Network: true`
header in the response, allowing the request. If set to `False`, the middleware will return a 400 response, blocking the request.

Adds signed cookie-based HTTP sessions. Session information is readable but not modifiable.
The session cookie is always set with the `"HttpOnly"` flag, preventing client-side JavaScript from accessing it.
Access or modify the session data using the `request.session` dictionary interface.

Changes to nested values are not tracked automatically. For example, `request.session["cart"].append(item)` does not mark the session as modified. Assign the updated value back to the session, such as `request.session["cart"] = cart`, to ensure the changes are saved.
* `max_age` - Session expiry time in seconds. Defaults to 2 weeks. If set to `None` then the cookie will last as long as the browser session.
* `same_site` - SameSite flag prevents the browser from sending session cookie along with cross-site requests. Defaults to `'lax'`.
* `path` - The path set for the session cookie. Defaults to `'/'`.

* `https_only` - Indicate that the `"Secure"` flag should be set (can be used with HTTPS only). Defaults to `False`. Set this to `True` in production to ensure the session cookie is only sent over HTTPS.

* `domain` - Domain of the cookie used to share cookie between subdomains or cross-domains. The browser defaults the domain to the same host that set the cookie, excluding subdomains ([reference](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Cookies#domain_attribute)).

* `partitioned` - Set the `Partitioned` flag when you write or clear the session cookie. Defaults to `False`. Set `https_only=True` when you enable it. For cross-site embeds, also set `same_site="none"`. This gives your embedded app a separate session for each top-level site ([reference](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Privacy/Guides/Third-party_cookies/Partitioned_cookies)).

Handles GZip responses for any request that includes `"gzip"` in the `Accept-Encoding` header.
The middleware will handle both standard and streaming responses.
On streaming responses, the middleware compresses and emits output for every chunk the application sends,
so chunks reach the client as they are produced instead of waiting for the compressor's buffer to fill.
This favors timely delivery over compression ratio: many small chunks compress less effectively than a few
large ones. Batch the chunks you yield if you want to maximize compression.
* `minimum_size` - Do not GZip responses that are smaller than this minimum size in bytes. Defaults to `500`.

* `compresslevel` - Used during GZip compression. It is an integer ranging from 1 to 9. Defaults to `9`. Lower value results in faster compression but larger file sizes, while higher value results in slower compression but smaller file sizes.

* `thread_minimum_size` - Compress body chunks at least this large in a worker thread, keeping the event loop responsive. Defaults to `131072` (128 KiB). Chunks below this size compress inline in at most a couple of milliseconds, while the fixed cost of dispatching to a worker thread would dominate.

* `exclude_content_types` - Content types that are never compressed. A response is excluded when its `Content-Type` media type equals one of these values, or matches a `type/*` entry like `"image/*"` - matching is case-insensitive and ignores parameters like `charset`. Defaults to `DEFAULT_EXCLUDED_CONTENT_TYPES` (importable, to extend rather than replace): `text/event-stream`, native gRPC (`application/grpc`, which also covers `application/grpc+proto` and other `application/grpc+...` subtypes), plus already-compressed formats - zip and gzip archives, common raster image types, `video/*`, `audio/*`, and WOFF fonts. `image/svg+xml` is deliberately not excluded, since SVG is text and compresses well.

Currently, the `BaseHTTPMiddleware` has some known limitations:

Starlette provides a `set_cookie` method to allow you to set cookies on the response object.
Signature: `Response.set_cookie(key, value, max_age=None, expires=None, path="/", domain=None, secure=False, httponly=False, samesite="lax", partitioned=False)`
* `key` - A string that will be the cookie's key.
* `value` - A string that will be the cookie's value.
* `max_age` - An integer that defines the lifetime of the cookie in seconds. A negative integer or a value of `0` will discard the cookie immediately. `Optional`
* `expires` - Either an integer that defines the number of seconds until the cookie expires, or a datetime. `Optional`
* `path` - A string that specifies the subset of routes to which the cookie will apply. `Optional`
* `domain` - A string that specifies the domain for which the cookie is valid. `Optional`
* `secure` - A bool indicating that the cookie will only be sent to the server if request is made using SSL and the HTTPS protocol. `Optional`
* `httponly` - A bool indicating that the cookie cannot be accessed via JavaScript through `Document.cookie` property, the `XMLHttpRequest` or `Request` APIs. `Optional`
* `samesite` - A string that specifies the samesite strategy for the cookie. Valid values are `'lax'`, `'strict'` and `'none'`. Defaults to `'lax'`. `Optional`

* `partitioned` - A bool that indicates to user agents that these cross-site cookies should only be available in the same top-level context that the cookie was first set in. Only available for Python 3.14+, otherwise an error will be raised. `Optional`
Conversely, Starlette also provides a `delete_cookie` method to manually expire a set cookie.
Signature: `Response.delete_cookie(key, path='/', domain=None, secure=False, httponly=False, samesite="lax", partitioned=False)`
To delete a partitioned cookie on Python 3.14+:
Pass `partitioned=True` to expire the cookie in the current partition. It defaults to `False`.
Use the same `path` and `domain` as the original cookie, within the same top-level site context.
Pass `secure=True` when deleting a partitioned cookie over HTTPS.
Browsers reject the expiration header if it includes `Partitioned` without `Secure`.

Starlette uses a thread pool in several scenarios to avoid blocking the event loop:
- When you create a synchronous endpoint using `def` instead of `async def`
- When running synchronous background tasks with [`BackgroundTask`](background.md)
- And some other scenarios that may not be documented...
Starlette will run your code in a thread pool to avoid blocking the event loop.

503|    def _parse_range_header(cls, http_range: str, file_size: int) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:

516|            return []
517|

519|
520|        if len(ranges) == 0:
521|            raise MalformedRangeHeader("Range header: range must be requested")
522|
523|        if any(not (0 <= start < file_size) for start, _ in ranges):
524|            raise RangeNotSatisfiable(file_size)
525|
526|        if any(start >= end for start, end in ranges):
527|            raise MalformedRangeHeader("Range header: start must be less than end")

529|        if len(ranges) == 1:
530|            return ranges
531|
532|        # Merge overlapping ranges

539|            else:

546|        ranges: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
547|
548|        for part in range_.split(","):
549|            part = part.strip()
550|
551|            # If the range is empty or a single dash, we ignore it.
552|            if not part or part == "-":
553|                continue
554|
555|            # If the range is not in the format "start-end", we ignore it.
556|            if "-" not in part:
557|                continue
558|
559|            start_str, end_str = part.split("-", 1)
560|            start_str = start_str.strip()
561|            end_str = end_str.strip()
562|
563|            try:
564|                start = int(start_str) if start_str else max(file_size - int(end_str), 0)
565|                end = int(end_str) + 1 if start_str and end_str and int(end_str) < file_size else file_size

573|    def generate_multipart(
574|        self,
575|        ranges: Sequence[tuple[int, int]],
576|        boundary: str,
577|        max_size: int,
578|        content_type: str,
579|    ) -> tuple[int, Callable[[int, int], bytes]]:
580|        r"""
581|        Multipart response headers generator.
582|
583|        ```
584|        --{boundary}\r\n
585|        Content-Type: {content_type}\r\n
586|        Content-Range: bytes {start}-{end-1}/{max_size}\r\n
587|        \r\n
588|        ..........content...........\r\n
589|        --{boundary}\r\n
590|        Content-Type: {content_type}\r\n
591|        Content-Range: bytes {start}-{end-1}/{max_size}\r\n
592|        \r\n
593|        ..........content...........\r\n
594|        --{boundary}--
595|        ```
596|        """
597|        boundary_len = len(boundary)
598|        static_header_part_len = 49 + boundary_len + len(content_type) + len(str(max_size))
599|        content_length = sum(
600|            (len(str(start)) + len(str(end - 1)) + static_header_part_len)  # Headers
601|            + (end - start)  # Content
602|            for start, end in ranges
603|        ) + (
604|            4 + boundary_len  # --boundary--
605|        )
606|        return (
607|            content_length,
608|            lambda start, end: (
609|                f"""\
610|--{boundary}\r
611|Content-Type: {content_type}\r
612|Content-Range: bytes {start}-{end - 1}/{max_size}\r
613|\r

47|def cookie_parser(cookie_string: str) -> dict[str, str]:
48|    """
49|    This function parses a ``Cookie`` HTTP header into a dict of key/value pairs.
50|
51|    It attempts to mimic browser cookie parsing behavior: browsers and web servers
52|    frequently disregard the spec (RFC 6265) when setting and reading cookies,
53|    so we attempt to suit the common scenarios here.
54|
55|    This function has been adapted from Django 3.1.0.
56|    Note: we are explicitly _NOT_ using `SimpleCookie.load` because it is based
57|    on an outdated spec and will fail on lots of input we want to support
58|    """
59|    cookie_dict: dict[str, str] = {}
60|    for chunk in cookie_string.split(";"):
61|        if "=" in chunk:
62|            key, val = chunk.split("=", 1)
63|        else:
64|            # Assume an empty name per
65|            # https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=169091
66|            key, val = "", chunk
67|        key, val = key.strip(), val.strip()
68|        if key or val:
69|            # unquote using Python's algorithm.
70|            cookie_dict[key] = http_cookies._unquote(val)
71|    return cookie_dict

116|def compile_path(
117|    path: str,
118|) -> tuple[Pattern[str], str, dict[str, Convertor[Any]]]:
119|    """
120|    Given a path string, like: "/{username:str}",
121|    or a host string, like: "{subdomain}.mydomain.org", return a three-tuple
122|    of (regex, format, {param_name:convertor}).
123|
124|    regex:      "/(?P<username>[^/]+)"
125|    format:     "/{username}"
126|    convertors: {"username": StringConvertor()}
127|    """
128|    is_host = not path.startswith("/")
129|
130|    path_regex = "^"
131|    path_format = ""
132|    duplicated_params: set[str] = set()
133|
134|    idx = 0
135|    param_convertors = {}
136|    for match in PARAM_REGEX.finditer(path):
137|        param_name, convertor_type = match.groups("str")
138|        convertor_type = convertor_type.lstrip(":")
139|        assert convertor_type in CONVERTOR_TYPES, f"Unknown path convertor '{convertor_type}'"
140|        convertor = CONVERTOR_TYPES[convertor_type]
141|
142|        path_regex += re.escape(path[idx : match.start()])
143|        path_regex += f"(?P<{param_name}>{convertor.regex})"
144|
145|        path_format += path[idx : match.start()]
146|        path_format += "{%s}" % param_name
147|
148|        if param_name in param_convertors:
149|            duplicated_params.add(param_name)
150|
151|        param_convertors[param_name] = convertor
152|
153|        idx = match.end()
154|
155|    if duplicated_params:
156|        names = ", ".join(sorted(duplicated_params))
157|        ending = "s" if len(duplicated_params) > 1 else ""
158|        raise ValueError(f"Duplicated param name{ending} {names} at path {path}")
159|
160|    if is_host:
161|        # Align with `Host.matches()` behavior, which ignores port.
162|        hostname = path[idx:]
163|        if not hostname.endswith("]"):
164|            hostname = hostname.rsplit(":", 1)[0]
165|        path_regex += re.escape(hostname) + "$"
166|    else:
167|        path_regex += re.escape(path[idx:]) + "$"
168|
169|    path_format += path[idx:]
170|
171|    # Host names are case-insensitive (RFC 9110, section 4.2.3).
172|    flags = re.IGNORECASE if is_host else 0
173|    return re.compile(path_regex, flags), path_format, param_convertors

609|                "use an @contextlib.asynccontextmanager function instead",
610|                StarletteDeprecationWarning,
611|            )
612|            self.lifespan_context = asynccontextmanager(lifespan)
613|        elif inspect.isgeneratorfunction(lifespan):
614|            warnings.warn(
615|                "generator function lifespans are deprecated, use an @contextlib.asynccontextmanager function instead",
616|                StarletteDeprecationWarning,
617|            )
618|            self.lifespan_context = _wrap_gen_lifespan_context(lifespan)
619|        else:

621|
622|        self.middleware_stack = self.app
623|        if middleware:

625|                self.middleware_stack = cls(self.middleware_stack, *args, **kwargs)
626|        if max_body_size is not None:

630|        if scope["type"] == "websocket":

632|            await websocket_close(scope, receive, send)

645|        for route in self.routes:

648|            except NoMatchFound:

652|    async def lifespan(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
653|        """
654|        Handle ASGI lifespan messages, which allows us to manage application
655|        startup and shutdown events.
656|        """
657|        started = False
658|        app: Any = scope.get("app")
659|        await receive()
660|        try:
661|            async with self.lifespan_context(app) as maybe_state:
662|                if maybe_state is not None:

39|            # (although most ASGI servers will just keep sending it)
40|            return {"type": "http.disconnect"}
41|        # wrapped_rcv state 1: consumed but not yet disconnected
42|        if self._wrapped_rcv_consumed:

44|            # is to send it a disconnect
45|            if self._is_disconnected:

47|                # since we know the client is disconnected no need to wait
48|                # for the message

50|                return {"type": "http.disconnect"}

82|class IdentityResponder:
83|    content_encoding: str

85|    def __init__(
86|        self,
87|        app: ASGIApp,
88|        minimum_size: int,
89|        *,
90|        exclude_content_types: tuple[str, ...] = DEFAULT_EXCLUDED_CONTENT_TYPES,

94|        self.exclude_content_types = _normalize_content_types(exclude_content_types)
95|        self.send: Send = unattached_send
96|        self.initial_message: Message = {}
97|        self.started = False
98|        self.content_encoding_set = False

106|    async def send_with_compression(self, message: Message) -> None:
107|        message_type = message["type"]

109|            # Don't send the initial message until we've determined how to
110|            # modify the outgoing headers correctly.
111|            self.initial_message = message
112|            message.setdefault("headers", [])
113|            headers = Headers(raw=self.initial_message["headers"])

115|            self.partial_response = message["status"] == 206
116|            media_type = headers.get("content-type", "").partition(";")[0].strip().lower()
117|            media_types = {media_type, media_type.partition("/")[0] + "/*"}
118|            if media_type.startswith("application/grpc+"):
119|                media_types.add("application/grpc")
120|            self.content_type_is_excluded = not media_types.isdisjoint(self.exclude_content_types)
121|            if self.content_encoding_set or self.partial_response or self.content_type_is_excluded:
122|                await self.send(self.initial_message)
123|        elif message_type in ("http.response.body", "http.response.pathsend") and (
124|            self.content_encoding_set or self.partial_response or self.content_type_is_excluded
125|        ):
126|            await self.send(message)
127|        elif message_type == "http.response.body" and not self.started:
128|            self.started = True
129|            body = message.get("body", b"")

131|            if len(body) < self.minimum_size and not more_body:
132|                # Don't apply compression to small outgoing responses.
133|                await self.send(self.initial_message)

135|            elif not more_body:
136|                # Standard response.
137|                body = await self.apply_compression(body, more_body=False)

139|                headers = MutableHeaders(raw=self.initial_message["headers"])
140|                headers.add_vary_header("Accept-Encoding")

142|                    headers["Content-Encoding"] = self.content_encoding
143|                    if self.initial_message.get("trailers", False):

147|                    message["body"] = body
148|
149|                await self.send(self.initial_message)
150|                await self.send(message)
151|            else:
152|                # Initial body in streaming response.
153|                body = await self.apply_compression(body, more_body=True)
154|
155|                headers = MutableHeaders(raw=self.initial_message["headers"])
156|                headers.add_vary_header("Accept-Encoding")
157|                if body != message["body"]:
158|                    headers["Content-Encoding"] = self.content_encoding
159|                    del headers["Content-Length"]
160|                    message["body"] = body
161|
162|                await self.send(self.initial_message)
163|                await self.send(message)
164|        elif message_type == "http.response.body":
165|            # Remaining body in streaming response.
166|            body = message.get("body", b"")
167|            more_body = message.get("more_body", False)
168|
169|            message["body"] = await self.apply_compression(body, more_body=more_body)
170|
171|            await self.send(message)
172|        elif message_type in ("http.response.early_hint", "http.response.trailers"):
173|            await self.send(message)
174|        elif message_type == "http.response.pathsend":  # pragma: no branch
175|            # Don't apply GZip to pathsend responses
176|            await self.send(self.initial_message)

180|        """Apply compression on the response body.
181|
182|        If more_body is False, the compression stream is finalized. Compression
183|        resources are only allocated once a body is actually compressed.
184|        """
185|        return body

188|class GZipResponder(IdentityResponder):
189|    content_encoding = "gzip"
190|
191|    def __init__(
192|        self,
193|        app: ASGIApp,
194|        minimum_size: int,
195|        compresslevel: int = 9,
196|        *,
197|        thread_minimum_size: int = 128 * 1024,  # 128 KiB
198|        exclude_content_types: tuple[str, ...] = DEFAULT_EXCLUDED_CONTENT_TYPES,

200|        super().__init__(app, minimum_size, exclude_content_types=exclude_content_types)

202|        self.compresslevel = compresslevel
203|        self.thread_minimum_size = thread_minimum_size

205|
206|    @property
207|    def compressor(self) -> zlib._Compress:
208|        if self._compressor is None:
209|            self._compressor = zlib.compressobj(self.compresslevel, zlib.DEFLATED, 16 + zlib.MAX_WBITS)
210|        return self._compressor
211|
212|    async def apply_compression(self, body: bytes, *, more_body: bool) -> bytes:
213|        if len(body) >= self.thread_minimum_size:
214|            # Compressing large chunks inline would block the event loop.
215|            limiter = _get_gzip_capacity_limiter()
216|            return await anyio.to_thread.run_sync(self._compress_body, body, more_body, limiter=limiter)

218|
219|    def _compress_body(self, body: bytes, more_body: bool) -> bytes:
220|        if more_body:
221|            return self.compressor.compress(body) + self.compressor.flush(zlib.Z_SYNC_FLUSH)

19|        assert scope["type"] == "http"
20|        self.scope = scope
21|        self.receive = receive

25|            for method in ("GET", "HEAD", "POST", "PUT", "PATCH", "DELETE", "OPTIONS", "QUERY")

31|        return self.dispatch().__await__()

36|

15|class CORSMiddleware:
16|    def __init__(

18|        app: ASGIApp,
19|        allow_origins: Collection[str] = (),
20|        allow_methods: Collection[str] = ("GET",),
21|        allow_headers: Collection[str] = (),
22|        allow_credentials: bool = False,
23|        allow_origin_regex: str | None = None,
24|        allow_private_network: bool = False,
25|        expose_headers: Collection[str] = (),
26|        max_age: int = 600,
27|    ) -> None:
28|        if "*" in allow_methods:
29|            allow_methods = ALL_METHODS
30|
31|        compiled_allow_origin_regex = None
32|        if allow_origin_regex is not None:
33|            compiled_allow_origin_regex = re.compile(allow_origin_regex)
34|
35|        allow_all_origins = "*" in allow_origins
36|        allow_all_headers = "*" in allow_headers

39|        simple_headers: dict[str, str] = {}

44|        if expose_headers:
45|            simple_headers["Access-Control-Expose-Headers"] = ", ".join(expose_headers)

49|        }
50|        if not preflight_explicit_allow_origin:
51|            preflight_headers["Access-Control-Allow-Origin"] = "*"
52|        preflight_headers.update(
53|            {
54|                "Access-Control-Allow-Methods": ", ".join(allow_methods),
55|                "Access-Control-Max-Age": str(max_age),
56|            }
57|        )
58|        allow_headers = sorted(SAFELISTED_HEADERS | set(allow_headers))
59|        if allow_headers and not allow_all_headers:
60|            preflight_headers["Access-Control-Allow-Headers"] = ", ".join(allow_headers)
61|        if allow_credentials:
62|            preflight_headers["Access-Control-Allow-Credentials"] = "true"
63|
64|        self.app = app
65|        self.allow_origins = allow_origins
66|        self.allow_methods = allow_methods
67|        self.allow_headers = [h.lower() for h in allow_headers]
68|        self.allow_all_origins = allow_all_origins
69|        self.allow_all_headers = allow_all_headers
70|        self.allow_credentials = allow_credentials
71|        self.preflight_explicit_allow_origin = preflight_explicit_allow_origin
72|        self.allow_origin_regex = compiled_allow_origin_regex
73|        self.allow_private_network = allow_private_network
74|        self.simple_headers = simple_headers
75|        self.preflight_headers = preflight_headers

77|    async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
78|        if scope["type"] != "http":  # pragma: no cover
79|            await self.app(scope, receive, send)
80|            return
81|
82|        method = scope["method"]
83|        headers = Headers(scope=scope)
84|        origin = headers.get("origin")
85|
86|        if origin is not None and method == "OPTIONS" and "access-control-request-method" in headers:
87|            response = self.preflight_response(request_headers=headers)
88|            await response(scope, receive, send)
89|            return
90|
91|        await self.simple_response(scope, receive, send, request_headers=headers)
92|
93|    def is_allowed_origin(self, origin: str) -> bool:
94|        if self.allow_all_origins:
95|            return True
96|
97|        if self.allow_origin_regex is not None and self.allow_origin_regex.fullmatch(origin):
98|            return True
99|
100|        return origin in self.allow_origins
101|
102|    def preflight_response(self, request_headers: Headers) -> Response:
103|        requested_origin = request_headers["origin"]
104|        requested_method = request_headers["access-control-request-method"]
105|        requested_headers = request_headers.get("access-control-request-headers")
106|        requested_private_network = request_headers.get("access-control-request-private-network")
107|
108|        headers = dict(self.preflight_headers)
109|        failures: list[str] = []
110|
111|        if self.is_allowed_origin(origin=requested_origin):
112|            if self.preflight_explicit_allow_origin:
113|                # The "else" case is already accounted for in self.preflight_headers
114|                # and the value would be "*".
115|                headers["Access-Control-Allow-Origin"] = requested_origin
116|        else:
117|            failures.append("origin")
118|
119|        if requested_method not in self.allow_methods:
120|            failures.append("method")
121|
122|        # If we allow all headers, then we have to mirror back any requested
123|        # headers in the response.
124|        if self.allow_all_headers and requested_headers is not None:
125|            headers["Access-Control-Allow-Headers"] = requested_headers
126|        elif requested_headers is not None:
127|            for header in [h.lower() for h in requested_headers.split(",")]:
128|                if header.strip() not in self.allow_headers:
129|                    failures.append("headers")
130|                    break
131|
132|        if requested_private_network is not None:
133|            if self.allow_private_network:
134|                headers["Access-Control-Allow-Private-Network"] = "true"
135|            else:
136|                failures.append("private-network")
137|
138|        # We don't strictly need to use 400 responses here, since its up to
139|        # the browser to enforce the CORS policy, but its more informative
140|        # if we do.
141|        if failures:
142|            failure_text = "Disallowed CORS " + ", ".join(failures)
143|            return PlainTextResponse(failure_text, status_code=400, headers=headers)
144|
145|        return PlainTextResponse("OK", status_code=200, headers=headers)
146|
147|    async def simple_response(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send, request_headers: Headers) -> None:
148|        send = functools.partial(self.send, send=send, request_headers=request_headers)
149|        await self.app(scope, receive, send)
150|
151|    async def send(self, message: Message, send: Send, request_headers: Headers) -> None:
152|        if message["type"] != "http.response.start":
153|            await send(message)
154|            return
155|
156|        message.setdefault("headers", [])
157|        headers = MutableHeaders(scope=message)
158|        origin = request_headers.get("Origin")
159|        if origin is not None:
160|            headers.update(self.simple_headers)
161|
162|        # If credentials are allowed, then we must respond with the specific origin instead of '*'.
163|        if origin is not None and self.allow_all_origins and self.allow_credentials:
164|            self.allow_explicit_origin(headers, origin)
165|
166|        # If we only allow specific origins, then we have to mirror back the Origin header in the response.
167|        elif origin is not None and not self.allow_all_origins and self.is_allowed_origin(origin=origin):
168|            self.allow_explicit_origin(headers, origin)
169|        else:
170|            headers["Vary"] = ", ".join([*headers.getlist("Vary"), "Origin"])
171|
172|        await send(message)
173|
174|    @staticmethod
175|    def allow_explicit_origin(headers: MutableHeaders, origin: str) -> None:
176|        headers["Access-Control-Allow-Origin"] = origin
177|        headers["Vary"] = ", ".join([*headers.getlist("Vary"), "Origin"])

27|            Pass a comma-separated string or a sequence. By default, exclude no URLs.

29|        meter_provider: Optional meter provider. If omitted, use the global meter provider.

31|
32|    def __init__(
33|        self,
34|        app: ASGIApp,
35|        *,
36|        excluded_urls: str | Sequence[str] = (),
37|        tracer_provider: trace.TracerProvider | None = None,
38|        meter_provider: metrics.MeterProvider | None = None,
39|    ) -> None:
40|        self.app = app
41|        self._meter_provider = meter_provider
42|        if isinstance(excluded_urls, str):
43|            excluded_urls = [pattern.strip() for pattern in excluded_urls.split(",")] if excluded_urls else ()
44|        self._excluded_urls = tuple(re.compile(pattern) for pattern in excluded_urls)
45|        self._tracer_provider = tracer_provider or trace.get_tracer_provider()

48|        if scope["type"] != "http" or scope.get("starlette.opentelemetry"):
49|            return await self.app(scope, receive, send)
50|
51|        scope["starlette.opentelemetry"] = True
52|        try:
53|            tracer_provider = self._tracer_provider
54|            if isinstance(tracer_provider, trace.NoOpTracerProvider):
55|                return await self.app(scope, receive, send)
56|
57|            url = URL(scope=scope)
58|            if any(pattern.search(str(url)) for pattern in self._excluded_urls):
59|                return await self.app(scope, receive, send)
60|
61|            original_method = scope.get("method", "")
62|            method = original_method.upper()
63|
64|            headers: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
65|            for name, value in scope.get("headers", []):
66|                headers.setdefault(name.decode("latin-1").lower(), []).append(value.decode("latin-1"))
67|

69|                "http.request.method": method,
70|                "url.path": scope.get("path", ""),
71|                "url.scheme": scope.get("scheme", "http"),
72|            }
73|            if original_method != method:
74|                attributes["http.request.method_original"] = original_method
75|            if url.query:
76|                attributes["url.query"] = url.query
77|            if url.hostname is not None:
78|                attributes["server.address"] = url.hostname
79|                server = scope.get("server")
80|                server_port = url.port if url.port is not None else server[1] if server is not None else None

40|    def get_endpoints(self, routes: list[BaseRoute]) -> list[EndpointInfo]:
41|        """

43|
44|        - path
45|            eg: /users/
46|        - http_method
47|            one of 'get', 'post', 'put', 'patch', 'delete', 'options', 'query'
48|        - func
49|            method ready to extract the docstring
50|        """
51|        endpoints_info: list[EndpointInfo] = []
52|
53|        for route in routes:
54|            if isinstance(route, Mount | Host):
55|                routes = route.routes or []
56|                if isinstance(route, Mount):
57|                    path = self._remove_converter(route.path)
58|                else:

60|                sub_endpoints = [
61|                    EndpointInfo(
62|                        path="".join((path, sub_endpoint.path)),
63|                        http_method=sub_endpoint.http_method,
64|                        func=sub_endpoint.func,
65|                    )
66|                    for sub_endpoint in self.get_endpoints(routes)
67|                ]

70|            elif not isinstance(route, Route) or not route.include_in_schema:
71|                continue
72|
73|            elif inspect.isfunction(route.endpoint) or inspect.ismethod(route.endpoint):
74|                path = self._remove_converter(route.path)
75|                for method in route.methods or ["GET"]:
76|                    if method == "HEAD":
77|                        continue
78|                    endpoints_info.append(EndpointInfo(path, method.lower(), route.endpoint))
79|            else:
80|                path = self._remove_converter(route.path)
81|                for method in ["get", "post", "put", "patch", "delete", "options", "query"]:
82|                    if not hasattr(route.endpoint, method):

84|                    func = getattr(route.endpoint, method)
85|                    endpoints_info.append(EndpointInfo(path, method.lower(), func))

95|        """
96|        return _remove_converter_pattern.sub("}", path)

98|    def parse_docstring(self, func_or_method: Callable[..., Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:

101|        """
102|        docstring = func_or_method.__doc__
103|        if not docstring:

110|        # the docstring.

123|        routes = request.app.routes

147|            if endpoint.path not in schema["paths"]:

149|

23|def wrap_app_handling_exceptions(app: ASGIApp, conn: Request | WebSocket) -> ASGIApp:
24|    exception_handlers: ExceptionHandlers
25|    status_handlers: StatusHandlers
26|    try:
27|        exception_handlers, status_handlers = conn.scope["starlette.exception_handlers"]
28|    except KeyError:
29|        exception_handlers, status_handlers = {}, {}
30|
31|    async def wrapped_app(scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
32|        response_started = False
33|
34|        async def sender(message: Message) -> None:
35|            nonlocal response_started
36|
37|            if message["type"] == "http.response.start":
38|                response_started = True
39|            await send(message)
40|
41|        try:
42|            await app(scope, receive, sender)
43|        except Exception as exc:
44|            handler = None
45|
46|            if isinstance(exc, HTTPException):
47|                handler = status_handlers.get(exc.status_code)
48|
49|            if handler is None:
50|                handler = _lookup_exception_handler(exception_handlers, exc)
51|
52|            if handler is None:
53|                raise exc
54|
55|            if response_started:
56|                raise RuntimeError("Caught handled exception, but response already started.") from exc
57|
58|            if is_async_callable(handler):
59|                response = await handler(conn, exc)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
60|            else:
61|                response = await run_in_threadpool(handler, conn, exc)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
62|            if response is not None:
63|                await response(scope, receive, sender)
64|            # Reused exception instances accumulate tracebacks across requests.
65|            exc.__traceback__ = None

127|class ServerErrorMiddleware:
128|    """
129|    Handles returning 500 responses when a server error occurs.
130|
131|    If 'debug' is set, then traceback responses will be returned,
132|    otherwise the designated 'handler' will be called.
133|
134|    This middleware class should generally be used to wrap *everything*
135|    else up, so that unhandled exceptions anywhere in the stack
136|    always result in an appropriate 500 response.
137|    """
138|
139|    def __init__(
140|        self,
141|        app: ASGIApp,
142|        handler: ExceptionHandler | None = None,
143|        debug: bool = False,
144|    ) -> None:
145|        self.app = app
146|        self.handler = handler
147|        self.debug = debug
148|
149|    async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
150|        if scope["type"] != "http":
151|            await self.app(scope, receive, send)
152|            return
153|
154|        response_started = False
155|
156|        async def _send(message: Message) -> None:
157|            nonlocal response_started, send
158|
159|            if message["type"] == "http.response.start":
160|                response_started = True
161|            await send(message)
162|
163|        try:
164|            await self.app(scope, receive, _send)
165|        except Exception as exc:
166|            request = Request(scope)
167|            if self.debug:
168|                # In debug mode, return traceback responses.
169|                response = await run_in_threadpool(self.debug_response, request, exc)
170|            elif self.handler is None:
171|                # Use our default 500 error handler.
172|                response = self.error_response(request, exc)
173|            else:
174|                # Use an installed 500 error handler.
175|                if is_async_callable(self.handler):
176|                    response = await self.handler(request, exc)  # type: ignore[assignment, arg-type]
177|                else:
178|                    response = await run_in_threadpool(self.handler, request, exc)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
179|
180|            if not response_started:
181|                await response(scope, receive, send)
182|
183|            # We always continue to raise the exception.
184|            # This allows servers to log the error, or allows test clients
185|            # to optionally raise the error within the test case.
186|            raise exc
187|
188|    def format_line(self, index: int, line: str, frame_lineno: int, frame_index: int) -> str:
189|        values = {
190|            # HTML escape - line could contain < or >
191|            "line": html.escape(line).replace(" ", "&nbsp"),
192|            "lineno": (frame_lineno - frame_index) + index,
193|        }
194|
195|        if index != frame_index:
196|            return LINE.format(**values)
197|        return CENTER_LINE.format(**values)
198|
199|    def generate_frame_html(self, frame: inspect.FrameInfo, is_collapsed: bool) -> str:
200|        code_context = "".join(
201|            self.format_line(
202|                index,
203|                line,
204|                frame.lineno,
205|                frame.index,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
206|            )
207|            for index, line in enumerate(frame.code_context or [])
208|        )
209|
210|        values = {
211|            # HTML escape - filename could contain < or >, especially if it's a virtual
212|            # file e.g. <stdin> in the REPL
213|            "frame_filename": html.escape(frame.filename),
214|            "frame_lineno": frame.lineno,
215|            # HTML escape - if you try very hard it's possible to name a function with <
216|            # or >
217|            "frame_name": html.escape(frame.function),
218|            "code_context": code_context,
219|            "collapsed": "collapsed" if is_collapsed else "",
220|            "collapse_button": "+" if is_collapsed else "‒",
221|        }
222|        return FRAME_TEMPLATE.format(**values)
223|
224|    def generate_html(self, exc: Exception, limit: int = 7) -> str:
225|        traceback_obj = traceback.TracebackException.from_exception(exc, capture_locals=True)
226|
227|        exc_html = ""
228|        is_collapsed = False
229|        exc_traceback = exc.__traceback__
230|        if exc_traceback is not None:
231|            frames = inspect.getinnerframes(exc_traceback, limit)
232|            for frame in reversed(frames):
233|                exc_html += self.generate_frame_html(frame, is_collapsed)
234|                is_collapsed = True
235|
236|        if sys.version_info >= (3, 13):  # pragma: no cover
237|            exc_type_str = traceback_obj.exc_type_str
238|        else:  # pragma: no cover
239|            exc_type_str = traceback_obj.exc_type.__name__
240|
241|        # escape error class and text
242|        error = f"{html.escape(exc_type_str)}: {html.escape(str(traceback_obj))}"
243|
244|        return TEMPLATE.format(styles=STYLES, js=JS, error=error, exc_html=exc_html)
245|
246|    def generate_plain_text(self, exc: Exception) -> str:
247|        return "".join(traceback.format_exception(type(exc), exc, exc.__traceback__))
248|
249|    def debug_response(self, request: Request, exc: Exception) -> Response:
250|        accept = request.headers.get("accept", "")
251|
252|        if "text/html" in accept:
253|            content = self.generate_html(exc)
254|            return HTMLResponse(content, status_code=500)
255|        content = self.generate_plain_text(exc)
256|        return PlainTextResponse(content, status_code=500)
257|
258|    def error_response(self, request: Request, exc: Exception) -> Response:
259|        return PlainTextResponse("Internal Server Error", status_code=500)

26|def build_environ(scope: Scope, body: bytes) -> dict[str, Any]:
27|    """
28|    Builds a scope and request body into a WSGI environ object.
29|    """
30|
31|    script_name = scope.get("root_path", "").encode("utf8").decode("latin1")
32|    path_info = scope["path"].encode("utf8").decode("latin1")
33|    if path_info == script_name or path_info.startswith(script_name.rstrip("/") + "/"):
34|        path_info = path_info[len(script_name) :]
35|
36|    environ = {
37|        "REQUEST_METHOD": scope["method"],
38|        "SCRIPT_NAME": script_name,
39|        "PATH_INFO": path_info,
40|        "QUERY_STRING": scope["query_string"].decode("ascii"),
41|        "SERVER_PROTOCOL": f"HTTP/{scope['http_version']}",
42|        "wsgi.version": (1, 0),
43|        "wsgi.url_scheme": scope.get("scheme", "http"),
44|        "wsgi.input": io.BytesIO(body),
45|        "wsgi.errors": sys.stdout,
46|        "wsgi.multithread": True,
47|        "wsgi.multiprocess": True,
48|        "wsgi.run_once": False,
49|    }
50|
51|    # Get server name and port - required in WSGI, not in ASGI
52|    server = scope.get("server") or ("localhost", 80)
53|    environ["SERVER_NAME"] = server[0]
54|    environ["SERVER_PORT"] = server[1]
55|
56|    # Get client IP address
57|    if scope.get("client"):
58|        environ["REMOTE_ADDR"] = scope["client"][0]
59|
60|    # Go through headers and make them into environ entries
61|    for name, value in scope.get("headers", []):
62|        name = name.decode("latin1")
63|        if name == "content-length":
64|            corrected_name = "CONTENT_LENGTH"
65|        elif name == "content-type":
66|            corrected_name = "CONTENT_TYPE"
67|        else:
68|            corrected_name = f"HTTP_{name}".upper().replace("-", "_")
69|        # HTTPbis say only ASCII chars are allowed in headers, but we latin1 just in
70|        # case
71|        value = value.decode("latin1")
72|        if corrected_name in environ:
73|            value = environ[corrected_name] + "," + value
74|        environ[corrected_name] = value
75|    return environ
76|
77|
78|class WSGIMiddleware:
79|    def __init__(self, app: Callable[..., Any]) -> None:
80|        self.app = app
81|
82|    async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
83|        assert scope["type"] == "http"
84|        responder = WSGIResponder(self.app, scope)
85|        await responder(receive, send)

88|class WSGIResponder:
89|    stream_send: ObjectSendStream[MutableMapping[str, Any]]
90|    stream_receive: ObjectReceiveStream[MutableMapping[str, Any]]
91|
92|    def __init__(self, app: Callable[..., Any], scope: Scope) -> None:
93|        self.app = app
94|        self.scope = scope
95|        self.status = None
96|        self.response_headers = None
97|        self.stream_send, self.stream_receive = anyio.create_memory_object_stream(math.inf)
98|        self.response_started = False
99|        self.exc_info: Any = None
100|
101|    async def __call__(self, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
102|        body = b""
103|        more_body = True
104|        while more_body:
105|            message = await receive()
106|            body += message.get("body", b"")
107|            more_body = message.get("more_body", False)
108|        environ = build_environ(self.scope, body)
109|
110|        async with create_collapsing_task_group() as task_group:
111|            task_group.start_soon(self.sender, send)
112|            async with self.stream_send:
113|                await anyio.to_thread.run_sync(self.wsgi, environ, self.start_response)
114|        if self.exc_info is not None:
115|            raise self.exc_info[0].with_traceback(self.exc_info[1], self.exc_info[2])
116|
117|    async def sender(self, send: Send) -> None:
118|        async with self.stream_receive:
119|            async for message in self.stream_receive:
120|                await send(message)
121|
122|    def start_response(
123|        self,
124|        status: str,
125|        response_headers: list[tuple[str, str]],
126|        exc_info: Any = None,
127|    ) -> None:
128|        self.exc_info = exc_info
129|        if not self.response_started:  # pragma: no branch
130|            self.response_started = True
131|            status_code_string, _ = status.split(" ", 1)
132|            status_code = int(status_code_string)
133|            headers = [
134|                (name.strip().encode("ascii").lower(), value.strip().encode("ascii"))
135|                for name, value in response_headers
136|            ]
137|            anyio.from_thread.run(
138|                self.stream_send.send,
139|                {
140|                    "type": "http.response.start",
141|                    "status": status_code,
142|                    "headers": headers,
143|                },
144|            )
145|
146|    def wsgi(
147|        self,
148|        environ: dict[str, Any],
149|        start_response: Callable[..., Any],
150|    ) -> None:
151|        for chunk in self.app(environ, start_response):
152|            anyio.from_thread.run(
153|                self.stream_send.send,
154|                {"type": "http.response.body", "body": chunk, "more_body": True},
155|            )
156|
157|        anyio.from_thread.run(self.stream_send.send, {"type": "http.response.body", "body": b""})

5|## 1.10.0 (October 24, 2026)
6|
7|#### Changed
8|
9|* Compare multidicts such as `FormData` and `QueryParams` by key while keeping the order of values under a repeated key, so `FormData` with repeated uploads no longer raises `TypeError`. `QueryParams("a=1&a=2")` and `QueryParams("a=2&a=1")` are no longer equal [#3619](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3619).
10|* Build URL-encoded form fields in the parser callbacks, lowering memory and CPU usage for forms with many fields [#3724](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3724).
11|* Compare `Match` members by identity during routing [#3665](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3665) and [#3722](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3722).
12|
13|#### Deprecated
14|
15|* Deprecate `starlette.formparsers.FormMessage`, which is no longer used [#3724](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3724).
16|
17|#### Fixed
18|
19|* Parse the last URL-encoded form field when the request stream ends without an empty chunk [#3599](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3599).
20|* Keep path parameter values that look like another placeholder in `url_path_for()` [#3725](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3725).
21|* Default omitted `http.response.start` headers in `BaseHTTPMiddleware`, `GZipMiddleware` and `SessionMiddleware` instead of raising `KeyError` [#3721](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3721).
22|* Clear the traceback of handled exceptions, so reused exception instances no longer keep per-request objects alive [#3205](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3205).
23|* Strip only one pair of matching outer quotes from `Config` env file values [#3720](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3720).
24|* Strip `root_path` from `PATH_INFO` only at a path segment boundary in `WSGIMiddleware` [#3718](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3718).
25|* Report NaN and infinity correctly in `FloatConvertor.to_string()` [#3716](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3716).
26|* Ignore `Range` on requests other than `GET` and `HEAD` in `FileResponse` [#3679](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3679).
27|
28|## 1.9.0 (October 18, 2026)
29|
30|#### Changed
31|
32|* Stream `TestClient` response bodies, so `client.stream()` returns before the application finishes. Closing an unfinished streamed response now cancels the application [#3491](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3491).
33|
34|#### Fixed
35|
36|* Percent-encode `?`, `#`, `\` and a leading `//` in the request path when building `request.url`, and `\` and a leading `//` in `url_path_for` [#3671](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3671).
37|* Use the byte length for `Content-Length` when the response body is a typed or multidimensional `memoryview` [#3622](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3622).
38|* Include `HEAD` in the `Allow` header of `HTTPEndpoint` 405 responses when `GET` is defined [#3585](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3585).
39|* Match host names case-insensitively in `Host` routing and `TrustedHostMiddleware` [#3542](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3542).
40|* Preserve every existing `Vary` header in `MutableHeaders.add_vary_header()`, used by `GZipMiddleware` and `SessionMiddleware` [#3675](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3675).

42|## 1.8.0 (October 13, 2026)
43|
44|This release drops Python 3.10 support and adds HTTP 103 Early Hints.
45|
46|#### Added
47|
48|* Add `Request.send_early_hints()` for HTTP 103 Early Hints through the ASGI `http.response.early_hint` extension [#3435](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3435).
49|
50|#### Changed
51|
52|* Require Python 3.11 or later, dropping support for Python 3.10 [#3592](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3592).
53|* Exclude native gRPC media types (`application/grpc` and `application/grpc+...`) from `GZipMiddleware` compression by default [#3565](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3565).
54|* Send `http.response.start` immediately in `GZipMiddleware` for responses with an existing `Content-Encoding`, status `206`, or an excluded content type, instead of waiting for the first body chunk [#3631](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3631).
55|* Resolve the multipart charset once per request instead of once per field [#3618](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3618).
56|
57|#### Fixed
58|
59|* Preserve response trailers through `GZipMiddleware` [#3565](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3565).
60|* Stop `FileResponse` transfers when the client disconnects [#3523](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3523).
61|* Stop multipart range responses when the file ends before a range is complete, instead of looping forever [#3583](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3583).
62|* Ignore `Range` when `If-Range` contains a weak ETag [#3567](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3567).
63|* Include `Allow: GET, HEAD` in `StaticFiles` `405` responses [#3640](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3640).
64|* Close `Request.stream()` generators deterministically, avoiding "Exception ignored" errors with stacked `BaseHTTPMiddleware` [#3628](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3628).
65|* Add `Vary: Cookie` when `Session.pop()` removes an existing key [#3186](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3186).
66|* Emit `Max-Age=0` on the session cookie when `SessionMiddleware` uses `max_age=0` [#3651](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3651).
67|* Bracket IPv6 hostnames in `URL.replace()` [#3617](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3617).

69|## 1.7.0 (September 23, 2026)
70|
71|This release adds experimental OpenTelemetry tracing and requires AnyIO 4.
72|
73|!!! warning "OpenTelemetryMiddleware is experimental"
74|    Its API and emitted telemetry may change in minor releases without a deprecation period
75|    [#3574](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3574).
76|
77|#### Added
78|
79|* Add experimental `OpenTelemetryMiddleware` for HTTP server spans, with URL exclusions and custom tracer providers [#3438](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3438), [#3463](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3463), and [#3520](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3520).
80|* Expose the matched route through `scope["route"]` [#3438](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3438).
81|* Support the `QUERY` HTTP method in `HTTPEndpoint`, CORS, and OpenAPI 3.2 schema generation [#3489](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3489).
82|* Capture HTTP response trailers in `TestClient` and expose them through `response.extensions["http.response.trailers"]` [#3563](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3563).
83|* Support partitioned cookies in `SessionMiddleware` [#3510](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3510).
84|* Add `partitioned` to `Response.delete_cookie()` on Python 3.14 and later [#3376](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3376).
85|* Support IPv6 hosts in `TrustedHostMiddleware` and `TestClient` [#3471](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3471).
86|* Support Python 3.15 [#3508](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3508).
87|
88|#### Changed
89|
90|* Require `anyio>=4.0.0,<5`, dropping support for AnyIO 3 [#3512](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3512).
91|* Raise `WebSocketDisconnected`, a `RuntimeError` subclass, for disconnected WebSocket operations [#2767](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/2767).
92|* Accept `Collection[str]` in `CORSMiddleware` configuration annotations, including sets and frozensets [#3518](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3518).
93|
94|#### Fixed
95|

329|## 0.52.0 (January 18, 2026)
330|
331|In this release, `State` can be accessed using dictionary-style syntax for improved type
332|safety ([#3036](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3036)).
333|
334|```python
335|from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
336|from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
337|from typing import TypedDict
338|
339|import httpx
340|
341|from starlette.applications import Starlette
342|from starlette.requests import Request
343|
344|
345|class State(TypedDict):
346|    http_client: httpx.AsyncClient
347|
348|
349|@asynccontextmanager
350|async def lifespan(app: Starlette) -> AsyncIterator[State]:
351|    async with httpx.AsyncClient() as client:
352|        yield {"http_client": client}
353|
354|
355|async def homepage(request: Request[State]):
356|    client = request.state["http_client"]
357|    # If you run the below line with mypy or pyright, it will reveal the correct type.
358|    reveal_type(client)  # Revealed type is 'httpx.AsyncClient'
359|```
360|
361|See [Accessing State](lifespan.md#accessing-state) for more details.

1473|### BaseHTTPMiddleware
1474|
1475|Added support for `BaseHTTPMiddleware`, which provides a standard
1476|request/response interface over a regular ASGI middleware.
1477|
1478|This means you can write ASGI middleware while still working at
1479|a request/response level, rather than handling ASGI messages directly.
1480|
1481|```python
1482|from starlette.applications import Starlette
1483|from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware
1484|
1485|
1486|class CustomMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware):
1487|    async def dispatch(self, request, call_next):
1488|        response = await call_next(request)
1489|        response.headers['Custom-Header'] = 'Example'
1490|        return response
1491|
1492|
1493|app = Starlette()
1494|app.add_middleware(CustomMiddleware)
1495|```

1497|## 0.6.0
1498|
1499|### request.path_params
1500|
1501|The biggest change in 0.6 is that endpoint signatures are no longer:
1502|
1503|```python
1504|async def func(request: Request, **kwargs) -> Response
1505|```
1506|
1507|Instead we just use:
1508|
1509|```python
1510|async def func(request: Request) -> Response
1511|```
1512|
1513|The path parameters are available on the request as `request.path_params`.
1514|
1515|This is different to most Python webframeworks, but I think it actually ends up
1516|being much more nicely consistent all the way through.
1517|
1518|### request.url_for()
1519|
1520|Request and WebSocketSession now support URL reversing with `request.url_for(name, **path_params)`.
1521|This method returns a fully qualified `URL` instance.
1522|The URL instance is a string-like object.
1523|
1524|### app.url_path_for()
1525|
1526|Applications now support URL path reversing with `app.url_path_for(name, **path_params)`.
1527|This method returns a `URL` instance with the path and scheme set.
1528|The URL instance is a string-like object, and will return only the path if coerced to a string.
1529|
1530|### app.routes
1531|
1532|Applications now support a `.routes` parameter, which returns a list of `[Route|WebSocketRoute|Mount]`.
1533|
1534|### Route, WebSocketRoute, Mount
1535|
1536|The low level components to `Router` now match the `@app.route()`, `@app.websocket_route()`, and `app.mount()` signatures.

1|
2|Starlette includes several middleware classes for adding behavior that is applied across
3|your entire application. These are all implemented as standard ASGI
4|middleware classes, and can be applied either to Starlette or to any other ASGI application.
5|
6|## Using middleware
7|
8|The Starlette application class allows you to include the ASGI middleware
9|in a way that ensures that it remains wrapped by the exception handler.
10|
11|```python
12|from starlette.applications import Starlette
13|from starlette.middleware import Middleware
14|from starlette.middleware.httpsredirect import HTTPSRedirectMiddleware
15|from starlette.middleware.trustedhost import TrustedHostMiddleware
16|
17|routes = ...
18|
19|# Ensure that all requests include an 'example.com' or
20|# '*.example.com' host header, and strictly enforce https-only access.
21|middleware = [
22|    Middleware(
23|        TrustedHostMiddleware,
24|        allowed_hosts=['example.com', '*.example.com'],
25|    ),
26|    Middleware(HTTPSRedirectMiddleware)
27|]
28|
29|app = Starlette(routes=routes, middleware=middleware)
30|```
31|
32|Every Starlette application automatically includes two pieces of middleware by default:
33|
34|* `ServerErrorMiddleware` - Ensures that application exceptions may return a custom 500 page, or display an application traceback in DEBUG mode. This is *always* the outermost middleware layer.
35|* `ExceptionMiddleware` - Adds exception handlers, so that particular types of expected exception cases can be associated with handler functions. For example raising `HTTPException(status_code=404)` within an endpoint will end up rendering a custom 404 page.
36|
37|Middleware is evaluated from top-to-bottom, so the flow of execution in our example
38|application would look like this:
39|
40|* Middleware
41|    * `ServerErrorMiddleware`
42|    * `TrustedHostMiddleware`
43|    * `HTTPSRedirectMiddleware`
44|    * `ExceptionMiddleware`
45|* Routing
46|* Endpoint
47|
48|The following middleware implementations are available in the Starlette package:
49|
50|## OpenTelemetry
51|
52|Creates an OpenTelemetry server span for every incoming HTTP request. The span follows the
53|OpenTelemetry HTTP semantic conventions, extracts distributed trace context from the request
54|headers, and uses the matched route template for its name and `http.route` attribute.
55|
56|!!! warning "Experimental API"
57|    `OpenTelemetryMiddleware` is experimental. Its API and emitted telemetry may change in minor
58|    releases without a deprecation period.
59|
60|Install the optional API dependency with `pip install opentelemetry-api`, or as part of
61|`pip install "starlette[full]"`. Starlette only uses the OpenTelemetry API. Your application
62|chooses and configures the SDK and exporter. If no tracer provider is configured, the middleware
63|skips tracing.
64|
65|**Pydantic Logfire** configures a global OpenTelemetry provider. Add the middleware to enable
66|Starlette tracing:
67|
68|```python
69|import logfire
70|
71|from starlette.applications import Starlette
72|from starlette.middleware import Middleware
73|from starlette.middleware.opentelemetry import OpenTelemetryMiddleware
74|
75|logfire.configure()
76|
77|app = Starlette(middleware=[Middleware(OpenTelemetryMiddleware)])
78|```
79|
80|The same applies to any standard OpenTelemetry SDK configuration:
81|
82|```python
83|from opentelemetry import trace
84|from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
85|from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import BatchSpanProcessor, ConsoleSpanExporter
86|
87|from starlette.applications import Starlette
88|from starlette.middleware import Middleware
89|from starlette.middleware.opentelemetry import OpenTelemetryMiddleware
90|
91|tracer_provider = TracerProvider()
92|tracer_provider.add_span_processor(BatchSpanProcessor(ConsoleSpanExporter()))
93|trace.set_tracer_provider(tracer_provider)
94|
95|app = Starlette(middleware=[Middleware(OpenTelemetryMiddleware)])
96|```
97|
98|You can create the app before you configure the global provider.
99|
100|You can also wrap any ASGI application directly:
101|
102|```python
103|from starlette.applications import Starlette
104|from starlette.middleware.opentelemetry import OpenTelemetryMiddleware
105|
106|app = OpenTelemetryMiddleware(Starlette())
107|```
108|
109|Multiple native middleware instances on the same request create only one span.
110|
111|### Exclude URLs
112|
113|Pass a comma-separated string or a sequence of regular expressions in `excluded_urls`. If any
114|expression matches the full request URL, the middleware does not create a span. This is useful for
115|health checks, readiness probes, and other high-volume endpoints that you do not need to trace.
116|
117|```python
118|from starlette.applications import Starlette
119|from starlette.middleware import Middleware
120|from starlette.middleware.opentelemetry import OpenTelemetryMiddleware
121|from starlette.requests import Request
122|from starlette.responses import PlainTextResponse
123|from starlette.routing import Route
124|
125|
126|async def homepage(request: Request) -> PlainTextResponse:
127|    return PlainTextResponse("Hello, world!")
128|
129|
130|app = Starlette(
131|    routes=[Route("/", homepage), Route("/health", homepage)],
132|    middleware=[
133|        Middleware(
134|            OpenTelemetryMiddleware,
135|            excluded_urls=r"/health$,/readiness$",
136|        )
137|    ],
138|)
139|```
