1312|        raise Exception("Exception")
1313|
1314|    def exception_with_context(request: Request) -> None:
1315|        try:
1316|            raise Exception("Inner exception")
1317|        except Exception:
1318|            raise Exception("Outer exception")
1319|
1320|    def exception_with_cause(request: Request) -> None:
1321|        try:
1322|            raise Exception("Inner exception")
1323|        except Exception as e:
1324|            raise Exception("Outer exception") from e

1326|    app = Starlette(

1329|            Route("/exception-with-context", endpoint=exception_with_context),
1330|            Route("/exception-with-cause", endpoint=exception_with_cause),
1331|        ],
1332|        middleware=[Middleware(PassthroughMiddleware)],
1333|    )

1335|

1337|    # but it is suppressed therefore not propagated to traceback.

1340|    assert str(ctx.value) == "Exception"
1341|    assert ctx.value.__cause__ is None

1345|    # For exceptions with context the context is propagated as a cause to avoid

1351|    assert str(ctx.value.__cause__) == "Inner exception"
1352|
1353|    # For exceptions with cause check that it gets correctly propagated.

1355|        client.get("/exception-with-cause")
1356|    assert str(ctx.value) == "Outer exception"

718|def test_lifespan_state_async_cm(test_client_factory: TestClientFactory) -> None:
719|    startup_complete = False
720|    shutdown_complete = False
721|
722|    class State(TypedDict):
723|        count: int
724|        items: list[int]
725|
726|    async def hello_world(request: Request) -> Response:
727|        # modifications to the state should not leak across requests
728|        assert request.state.count == 0
729|        # modify the state, this should not leak to the lifespan or other requests
730|        request.state.count += 1
731|        # since state.items is a mutable object this modification _will_ leak across
732|        # requests and to the lifespan
733|        request.state.items.append(1)
734|        return PlainTextResponse("hello, world")
735|
736|    @contextlib.asynccontextmanager
737|    async def lifespan(app: Starlette) -> AsyncIterator[State]:
738|        nonlocal startup_complete, shutdown_complete
739|        startup_complete = True
740|        state = State(count=0, items=[])
741|        yield state
742|        shutdown_complete = True
743|        # modifications made to the state from a request do not leak to the lifespan
744|        assert state["count"] == 0
745|        # unless of course the request mutates a mutable object that is referenced
746|        # via state
747|        assert state["items"] == [1, 1]
748|
749|    app = Router(
750|        lifespan=lifespan,
751|        routes=[Route("/", hello_world)],
752|    )
753|
754|    assert not startup_complete
755|    assert not shutdown_complete
756|    with test_client_factory(app) as client:
757|        assert startup_complete
758|        assert not shutdown_complete
759|        client.get("/")
760|        # Calling it a second time to ensure that the state is preserved.
761|        client.get("/")
762|    assert startup_complete
763|    assert shutdown_complete

37|    # anyio's TaskInfo comparisons are invalid after their associated native

90|def test_use_testclient_as_contextmanager(test_client_factory: TestClientFactory, anyio_backend_name: str) -> None:
91|    """
92|    This test asserts a number of properties that are important for an
93|    app level task_group
94|    """
95|    counter = itertools.count()
96|    identity_runvar = anyio.lowlevel.RunVar[int]("identity_runvar")
97|
98|    def get_identity() -> int:
99|        try:
100|            return identity_runvar.get()
101|        except LookupError:
102|            token = next(counter)
103|            identity_runvar.set(token)
104|            return token
105|
106|    startup_task = object()
107|    startup_loop = None
108|    shutdown_task = object()
109|    shutdown_loop = None
110|
111|    @asynccontextmanager
112|    async def lifespan_context(app: Starlette) -> AsyncGenerator[None, None]:
113|        nonlocal startup_task, startup_loop, shutdown_task, shutdown_loop
114|
115|        startup_task = current_task()
116|        startup_loop = get_identity()
117|        async with anyio.create_task_group():
118|            yield
119|        shutdown_task = current_task()
120|        shutdown_loop = get_identity()
121|
122|    async def loop_id(request: Request) -> JSONResponse:
123|        return JSONResponse(get_identity())
124|
125|    app = Starlette(
126|        lifespan=lifespan_context,
127|        routes=[Route("/loop_id", endpoint=loop_id)],
128|    )
129|
130|    client = test_client_factory(app)
131|
132|    with client:
133|        # within a TestClient context every async request runs in the same thread
134|        assert client.get("/loop_id").json() == 0
135|        assert client.get("/loop_id").json() == 0
136|
137|    # that thread is also the same as the lifespan thread
138|    assert startup_loop == 0
139|    assert shutdown_loop == 0
140|
141|    # lifespan events run in the same task, this is important because a task
142|    # group must be entered and exited in the same task.
143|    assert startup_task is shutdown_task
144|
145|    # outside the TestClient context, new requests continue to spawn in new
146|    # event loops in new threads
147|    assert client.get("/loop_id").json() == 1
148|    assert client.get("/loop_id").json() == 2
149|
150|    first_task = startup_task
151|
152|    with client:
153|        # the TestClient context can be re-used, starting a new lifespan task
154|        # in a new thread
155|        assert client.get("/loop_id").json() == 3
156|        assert client.get("/loop_id").json() == 3
157|
158|    assert startup_loop == 3
159|    assert shutdown_loop == 3
160|
161|    # lifespan events still run in the same task, with the context but...
162|    assert startup_task is shutdown_task
163|
164|    # ... the second TestClient context creates a new lifespan task.
165|    assert first_task is not startup_task

211|def test_websocket_concurrency_pattern(test_client_factory: TestClientFactory) -> None:
212|    stream_send: ObjectSendStream[MutableMapping[str, Any]]
213|    stream_receive: ObjectReceiveStream[MutableMapping[str, Any]]
214|    stream_send, stream_receive = anyio.create_memory_object_stream()
215|
216|    async def reader(websocket: WebSocket) -> None:
217|        async with stream_send:
218|            async for data in websocket.iter_json():
219|                await stream_send.send(data)
220|
221|    async def writer(websocket: WebSocket) -> None:
222|        async with stream_receive:
223|            async for message in stream_receive:
224|                await websocket.send_json(message)
225|
226|    async def app(scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
227|        websocket = WebSocket(scope, receive=receive, send=send)
228|        await websocket.accept()
229|        async with anyio.create_task_group() as task_group:
230|            task_group.start_soon(reader, websocket)
231|            await writer(websocket)
232|        await websocket.close()
233|
234|    client = test_client_factory(app)
235|    with client.websocket_connect("/") as websocket:
236|        websocket.send_json({"hello": "world"})
237|        data = websocket.receive_json()

136|def test_gzip_streaming_compression_in_thread(test_client_factory: TestClientFactory) -> None:
137|    chunk = hashlib.shake_256(b"starlette-gzip-stream").digest(256 * 1024)
138|
139|    async def app(scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:

141|        await send({"type": "http.response.body", "body": chunk, "more_body": True})
142|        await send({"type": "http.response.body", "body": b"tail"})

144|    # Ensure the streamed chunk takes the worker-thread compression path.
145|    middleware = GZipMiddleware(app, thread_minimum_size=len(chunk))
146|    events: list[Message] = []
147|

159|    assert response.headers["Content-Encoding"] == "gzip"
160|

163|    assert decompressor.decompress(events[1]["body"]) == chunk
164|    assert decompressor.decompress(events[2]["body"]) == b"tail"

150|def make_json_payload(size: int) -> bytes:
151|    """Build a deterministic, valid JSON document of exactly ``size`` bytes."""
152|    prefix = b'{"requests":['
153|    padding_prefix = b'],"padding":"'
154|    suffix = b'"}'
155|    output = io.BytesIO()
156|    output.write(prefix)
157|
158|    index = 0
159|    while True:
160|        row = json.dumps(
161|            {
162|                "id": index,
163|                "timestamp": f"2026-08-04T12:{index % 60:02d}:{index * 7 % 60:02d}.{index * 997 % 1000:03d}Z",
164|                "method": ("GET", "POST", "PATCH", "DELETE")[index % 4],
165|                "path": f"/api/v1/projects/{index % 1_009}/events/{index * 17 % 65_537}",
166|                "status": (200, 201, 204, 400, 404, 409, 422, 500)[index % 8],
167|                "duration_ms": round((index * 37 % 10_000) / 100, 2),
168|                "request_id": f"{index * 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15 % (1 << 128):032x}",
169|                "message": ("request completed", "validation failed", "resource updated")[index % 3],
170|            },
171|            separators=(",", ":"),
172|        ).encode()
173|        separator = b"," if index else b""
174|        required_tail = len(padding_prefix) + len(suffix)
175|        if output.tell() + len(separator) + len(row) + required_tail > size:
176|            break
177|        output.write(separator)
178|        output.write(row)
179|        index += 1
180|
181|    output.write(padding_prefix)
182|    output.write(b"x" * (size - output.tell() - len(suffix)))
183|    output.write(suffix)
184|    payload = output.getvalue()
185|    assert len(payload) == size
186|    return payload

189|def make_text_payload(size: int) -> bytes:
190|    paragraph = (
191|        b"Starlette is a lightweight ASGI framework/toolkit, which is ideal for building async web services in Python. "
192|        b"It is production-ready and gives you the following: seriously impressive performance, WebSocket support, "
193|        b"in-process background tasks, startup and shutdown events, and a test client built on HTTPX.\n"
194|    )
195|    return (paragraph * (size // len(paragraph) + 1))[:size]

198|def make_payload(kind: PayloadKind, size: int) -> bytes:
199|    if kind == "json":
200|        return make_json_payload(size)
201|    if kind == "text":
202|        return make_text_payload(size)
203|    # SHAKE provides deterministic high-entropy bytes without keeping another
204|    # 10 MiB random-data buffer alive alongside the returned payload.
205|    return hashlib.shake_256(b"starlette-gzip-benchmark-v1").digest(size)

208|def make_bypass_messages(case: BypassCase) -> tuple[Message, ...]:
209|    headers = [(b"content-type", b"application/json"), (b"content-length", str(case.body_size).encode())]
210|    if case.reason == "content-encoding":
211|        headers.append((b"content-encoding", b"br"))
212|    elif case.reason == "event-stream":
213|        headers[0] = (b"content-type", b"text/event-stream")
214|
215|    response_start: Message = {"type": "http.response.start", "status": 200, "headers": headers}
216|    if case.reason == "pathsend":
217|        response_body: Message = {"type": "http.response.pathsend", "path": "/tmp/starlette-benchmark"}
218|    else:
219|        response_body = {"type": "http.response.body", "body": b"x" * case.body_size}
220|    return response_start, response_body

71|class MultipartApp:
72|    def __init__(self, case: BenchmarkCase) -> None:
73|        self.case = case
74|
75|    async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
76|        request = Request(scope, receive)
77|        try:
78|            async with request.form(
79|                max_files=self.case.max_files,
80|                max_fields=self.case.max_fields,
81|                max_part_size=self.case.max_part_size,
82|            ) as form:
83|                fields = 0
84|                files = 0
85|                file_bytes = 0
86|                for _, value in form.multi_items():
87|                    if isinstance(value, UploadFile):
88|                        files += 1
89|                        assert value.size is not None
90|                        file_bytes += value.size
91|                    else:
92|                        fields += 1
93|        except MultiPartException as exc:
94|            await send_result(send, 400, exc.message.encode())
95|            return
96|
97|        await send_result(send, 200, f"{fields}:{files}:{file_bytes}".encode())

100|def http_scope() -> Scope:
101|    return {
102|        "type": "http",
103|        "asgi": {"version": "3.0", "spec_version": "2.5"},
104|        "http_version": "1.1",
105|        "method": "POST",
106|        "scheme": "http",
107|        "path": "/",
108|        "raw_path": b"/",
109|        "root_path": "",
110|        "query_string": b"",
111|        "headers": [(b"content-type", CONTENT_TYPE)],
112|        "client": ("127.0.0.1", 50000),
113|        "server": ("127.0.0.1", 80),
114|    }
115|
116|
117|def field_part(index: int, size: int) -> bytes:
118|    value = bytes((65 + index % 26,)) * size
119|    return (
120|        b"--"
121|        + BOUNDARY
122|        + b'\r\nContent-Disposition: form-data; name="field'
123|        + str(index).encode()
124|        + b'"\r\n\r\n'
125|        + value
126|        + b"\r\n"
127|    )
128|
129|
130|def file_part(index: int, size: int, boundary_like: bool) -> bytes:
131|    if boundary_like:
132|        marker = b"\r\n--" + BOUNDARY[:-1] + b"x"
133|        content = (marker * (size // len(marker) + 1))[:size]
134|    else:
135|        content = bytes((65 + index % 26,)) * size
136|    return (
137|        b"--"
138|        + BOUNDARY
139|        + b'\r\nContent-Disposition: form-data; name="file'
140|        + str(index).encode()
141|        + b'"; filename="file.bin"\r\nContent-Type: application/octet-stream\r\n\r\n'
142|        + content
143|        + b"\r\n"
144|    )
145|
146|
147|def make_body(case: BenchmarkCase) -> bytes:
148|    parts = [field_part(index, case.field_size) for index in range(case.fields)]
149|    parts.extend(file_part(index, size, case.boundary_like) for index, size in enumerate(case.file_sizes))
150|    if case.malformed:
151|        parts.append(b"--" + BOUNDARY + b"\r\nContent-Disposition: form-data\r\n\r\ninvalid\r\n")
152|    parts.append(b"--" + BOUNDARY + b"--\r\n")
153|    return b"".join(parts)
154|
155|
156|def make_chunks(body: bytes, chunk_size: int | None) -> tuple[bytes, ...]:
157|    if chunk_size is None:
158|        return (body,)
159|    return tuple(body[offset : offset + chunk_size] for offset in range(0, len(body), chunk_size))
160|
161|
162|def dispatch(runner: ASGIRunner, app: ASGIApp, chunks: tuple[bytes, ...]) -> list[Message]:
163|    return runner.run(app, http_scope(), ChunkedReceive(chunks))

1|# Benchmarks
2|
3|## Minimal response dispatch
4|
5|The response benchmark measures a two-byte response through progressively larger
6|parts of the public stack: raw ASGI, a prebuilt `Response`, a newly constructed
7|`Response`, a single `Route`, and a complete `Starlette` application. The raw
8|ASGI case is the control for event-loop and message-capture overhead.
9|
10|Each dispatch receives a fresh ASGI scope. The application cases are warmed
11|before measurement so lazy middleware construction and interpreter specialization
12|are not attributed to every request.
13|
14|Run it locally with:
15|
16|```console
17|uv run pytest benchmarks/response_benchmark.py --codspeed
18|```
19|
20|## Request bodies
21|
22|The request benchmark compares `Request.body()` with `Request.stream()` for
23|1 KiB, 1 MiB, and 10 MiB payloads. The larger payloads are delivered both as a
24|single ASGI message and in 64 KiB chunks to separate byte volume from
25|per-message overhead.
26|
27|Payload and chunk construction happen outside the measured region. Every
28|dispatch creates a fresh `Request`, ASGI scope, and receive callable. The
29|response reports the consumed byte count, which is validated after measurement.
30|
31|Run it locally with:
32|
33|```console
34|uv run pytest benchmarks/request_benchmark.py --codspeed
35|```
36|
37|## JSON
38|
39|The JSON benchmark measures `Request.json()` and `JSONResponse` with structured
40|payloads of approximately 1 KiB and 1 MiB. The large request is delivered both
41|as a single ASGI message and in 64 KiB chunks.
42|
43|Payload encoding and chunk construction happen outside the measured region.
44|Request decoding and response encoding happen inside it, and each result is
45|validated after measurement.
46|
47|Run it locally with:
48|
49|```console
50|uv run pytest benchmarks/json_benchmark.py --codspeed
51|```
52|
53|## URL-encoded forms
54|
55|The URL-encoded benchmark measures `Request.form()` with 1,000 fields, a large
56|field, percent-encoded data, and field-count and part-size limit failures. The
57|large field is delivered as a single ASGI message and in 64 KiB chunks.
58|
59|Run it locally with:
60|
61|```console
62|uv run pytest benchmarks/urlencoded_benchmark.py --codspeed
63|```
64|
65|## Streaming responses
66|
67|The streaming benchmark measures `StreamingResponse` with 1 KiB and 1 MiB
68|bodies. The large body uses 1 KiB, 64 KiB, and single-chunk delivery to expose
69|the per-chunk dispatch cost.
70|
71|Run it locally with:
72|
73|```console
74|uv run pytest benchmarks/streaming_response_benchmark.py --codspeed
75|```
76|
77|## File responses
78|
79|The file benchmark measures `FileResponse` with fallback reads,
80|`http.response.pathsend`, and a single byte range. File creation happens outside
81|the measured region, while response construction, stat, and delivery happen
82|inside it.
83|
84|Run it locally with:
85|
86|```console
87|uv run pytest benchmarks/file_response_benchmark.py --codspeed
88|```
89|
90|## WebSockets
91|
92|The WebSocket benchmark measures complete text, bytes, and JSON echo exchanges
93|through the public `WebSocket` API. Each dispatch includes connect, accept,
94|receive, send, and close state transitions.
95|
96|Run it locally with:
97|
98|```console
99|uv run pytest benchmarks/websocket_benchmark.py --codspeed
100|```
101|
102|## Multipart forms
103|
104|The multipart benchmark measures `Request.form()` with field-heavy, in-memory
105|file, spooled file, mixed form, and boundary-like payloads. It also covers
106|malformed forms and field, file, and part-size limit failures.
107|
108|File workloads use 64 KiB ASGI chunks. The 10 MiB file also has a single-message
109|control case. Multipart body and chunk construction happen outside the measured
110|region, while parsing and upload cleanup happen inside it.
111|
112|Run it locally with:
113|
114|```console
115|uv run pytest benchmarks/multipart_benchmark.py --codspeed
116|```
117|
118|On Linux with glibc, you can use the same allocator setting as CI:
119|
120|```console
121|GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.malloc.mmap_threshold=32768 PYTHONHASHSEED=0 uv run pytest benchmarks/multipart_benchmark.py --codspeed
122|```
123|
124|glibc normally adjusts the
125|[`mmap` threshold](https://sourceware.org/glibc/manual/2.39/html_node/Memory-Allocation-Tunables.html)
126|based on earlier allocations. This can make an upload buffer grow in place
127|in one run and require a copy in another. CI fixes the threshold at 32 KiB,
128|below the 64 KiB upload chunks, to reduce this variation. Allocation, parsing,
129|and cleanup stay inside the measured region. Changing this setting shifts
130|the simulation baseline, so compare runs that use the same setting.
131|
132|## Routing
133|
134|The routing benchmark exercises `Router` dispatch through its ASGI interface
135|against a synthetic REST-style route table (120 routes as 30 resource groups
136|of four routes each, plus a 20-route variant for small applications).
137|
138|The scenarios pin down the cases that scale differently with table size:
139|a static hit on an early route, a static and a parameterized hit on the last
140|routes, a full miss, and a wrong-method request (`405`). Each measured call
141|dispatches one request through the router, with a fresh ASGI scope built per
142|dispatch so CodSpeed warmup runs cannot pollute the measured one; response
143|status is validated on the benchmark's return value, outside the measured
144|region.
145|
146|Run it locally with:
147|
148|```console
149|uv run pytest benchmarks/routing_benchmark.py --codspeed
150|```
151|
152|## GZip
153|
154|The gzip benchmark exercises Starlette's `GZipMiddleware` through its ASGI
155|interface with deterministic payloads representing valid JSON, repetitive
156|text, and incompressible bytes.
157|
158|It compares levels 1 through 9 at 1 MiB. It also compares representative levels
159|1, 6, and 9 at 32 KiB, 256 KiB, 5 MiB, and 10 MiB. This keeps the suite useful
160|for detecting payload-size regressions without running the full Cartesian
161|product of every level and large size.
162|
163|Run it locally with:
164|
165|```console
166|uv run pytest benchmarks/gzip_benchmark.py --codspeed
167|```
168|
169|Payload construction, middleware configuration, and decompression validation
170|are outside the measured region. The measured call includes responder
171|construction, fresh mutable ASGI message containers, header handling,
172|compression, and resource cleanup. Recreating the message containers prevents
173|CodSpeed warmups from mutating the response used by the measured invocation.
174|Each case creates only one input payload, so the largest case does not leave all
175|benchmark inputs resident in memory. CodSpeed CI records simulated CPU
176|performance, peak heap usage, and allocation counts.
177|
178|The end-to-end bypass benchmarks run the complete `GZipMiddleware` ASGI path
179|for responses below `minimum_size`, responses with an existing
180|`Content-Encoding`, `text/event-stream` responses, and
181|`http.response.pathsend`. Their response payloads are also constructed outside
182|the measured region, isolating middleware allocation overhead.
183|
184|The responsiveness benchmark schedules a 10 MiB JSON response immediately
185|before a tiny response that bypasses compression. CodSpeed measures the work
186|needed for the tiny response to complete, then drains and validates the large
187|response outside the measured region. This provides a stable CPU-simulation
188|benchmark for detecting event-loop starvation without relying on wall-clock
189|timing or concurrent request storms. The existing `json-10MiB-level-9`
190|compression case separately measures the large response's total completion.

19|class BodyApp:

26|    async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
27|        length = 0
28|        async for chunk in Request(scope, receive).stream():
29|            length += len(chunk)

34|    await send({"type": "http.response.start", "status": 200, "headers": []})
35|    await send({"type": "http.response.body", "body": str(length).encode()})

38|@dataclass(frozen=True)
39|class BenchmarkCase:
40|    mode: ReadMode
41|    body_size: int
42|    chunk_size: int
43|
44|    @property
45|    def id(self) -> str:
46|        body_size = format_size(self.body_size)
47|        chunk_size = "single" if self.chunk_size == self.body_size else format_size(self.chunk_size)
48|        return f"{self.mode}-{body_size}-{chunk_size}"
49|
50|
51|READ_MODES: tuple[ReadMode, ...] = ("body", "stream")
52|BODY_CASES = (
53|    (KiB, KiB),
54|    (MiB, MiB),
55|    (MiB, 64 * KiB),
56|    (10 * MiB, 10 * MiB),
57|    (10 * MiB, 64 * KiB),
58|)
59|CASES = tuple(BenchmarkCase(mode, body_size, chunk_size) for mode in READ_MODES for body_size, chunk_size in BODY_CASES)
60|APPS: dict[ReadMode, ASGIApp] = {"body": BodyApp(), "stream": StreamApp()}
61|

63|def format_size(size: int) -> str:
64|    if size >= MiB:

66|    return f"{size // KiB}KiB"

1|from __future__ import annotations
2|
3|from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
4|from dataclasses import dataclass
5|
6|import pytest
7|from pytest_codspeed.plugin import BenchmarkFixture
8|
9|from benchmarks._utils import ASGIRunner
10|from starlette.responses import StreamingResponse
11|from starlette.types import ASGIApp, Message, Receive, Scope, Send
12|
13|KiB = 1024
14|MiB = 1024 * KiB
15|
16|
17|@dataclass(frozen=True)
18|class BenchmarkCase:
19|    id: str
20|    body_size: int
21|    chunk_size: int
22|
23|
24|CASES = (
25|    BenchmarkCase("1KiB-single", KiB, KiB),
26|    BenchmarkCase("1MiB-1KiB", MiB, KiB),
27|    BenchmarkCase("1MiB-64KiB", MiB, 64 * KiB),
28|    BenchmarkCase("1MiB-single", MiB, MiB),
29|)
30|
31|
32|class StreamingApp:
33|    def __init__(self, chunks: tuple[bytes, ...]) -> None:
34|        self.chunks = chunks
35|
36|    async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
37|        await StreamingResponse(iter_chunks(self.chunks))(scope, receive, send)
38|
39|
40|async def iter_chunks(chunks: tuple[bytes, ...]) -> AsyncIterator[bytes]:
41|    for chunk in chunks:
42|        yield chunk
43|
44|
45|def make_chunks(body_size: int, chunk_size: int) -> tuple[bytes, ...]:
46|    payload = b"x" * body_size
47|    return tuple(payload[offset : offset + chunk_size] for offset in range(0, body_size, chunk_size))
48|
49|
50|def http_scope() -> Scope:
51|    return {
52|        "type": "http",
53|        "asgi": {"version": "3.0", "spec_version": "2.5"},
54|        "http_version": "1.1",
55|        "method": "GET",
56|        "scheme": "http",
57|        "path": "/",
58|        "raw_path": b"/",
59|        "root_path": "",
60|        "query_string": b"",
61|        "headers": [],
62|        "client": ("127.0.0.1", 50000),
63|        "server": ("127.0.0.1", 80),
64|    }
65|
66|
67|def dispatch(runner: ASGIRunner, app: ASGIApp) -> list[Message]:
68|    return runner.run(app, http_scope())
69|
70|
71|@pytest.fixture(scope="module", autouse=True)
72|def warm_streaming(asgi_runner: ASGIRunner) -> None:
73|    app = StreamingApp((b"x",))
74|    for _ in range(100):
75|        dispatch(asgi_runner, app)
76|
77|
78|@pytest.mark.parametrize("case", CASES, ids=lambda case: case.id)
79|@pytest.mark.benchmark(max_time=0.5, max_rounds=1)
80|def test_streaming_response(asgi_runner: ASGIRunner, benchmark: BenchmarkFixture, case: BenchmarkCase) -> None:
81|    chunks = make_chunks(case.body_size, case.chunk_size)
82|    messages = benchmark.pedantic(dispatch, args=(asgi_runner, StreamingApp(chunks)), rounds=1)
83|
84|    assert messages[0] == {"type": "http.response.start", "status": 200, "headers": []}
85|    assert messages[-1] == {"type": "http.response.body", "body": b"", "more_body": False}
86|    assert len(messages) == len(chunks) + 2
87|    assert sum(len(message.get("body", b"")) for message in messages[1:]) == case.body_size
88|    assert all(message.get("more_body") is True for message in messages[1:-1])
89|    benchmark.extra_info["body_bytes"] = case.body_size
90|    benchmark.extra_info["chunk_bytes"] = case.chunk_size
91|    benchmark.extra_info["chunks"] = len(chunks)
